title: U.S. House · Florida's 5th District
area: Northeast Florida including most of Jacksonville (Duval County).

context.text: Incumbent John Rutherford defeated Mark Kaye in the August 18, 2026 Republican primary. Rachel Grage won the Democratic primary over Alexander Hazen and Mark Heggestad. William Upham is a write-in, no-party-affiliation candidate.

candidates.name: John Rutherford
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Republican primary over Mark Kaye.

summary.text: John Rutherford is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Florida's 5th District. A former Jacksonville police officer, he was elected Duval County sheriff three times before winning an open House seat in 2016. He serves on the House Appropriations Committee and is seeking another term.

background.text: Born in Omaha, Nebraska, in 1952; according to his congressional biography, he has lived in Jacksonville since 1958.

Earned an associate degree from Florida Junior College (1972) and a bachelor's degree in criminology from Florida State University (1974); he is also a graduate of the FBI National Academy (171st Session) and the National Executive Institute.
Began his law enforcement career in 1974 as a patrolman with the Jacksonville Sheriff's Office and worked up to sheriff.

Elected Sheriff of Duval County in 2003, 2007, and 2011, running a 3,200-employee office for twelve years. His congressional biography says he emphasized intelligence-led, community-based policing and mental-health aspects of the criminal justice system.
Served as chair of the Legislative Committee of the Florida Sheriffs Association.

Won the open Florida 4th District seat in 2016 (38.7% in a seven-candidate Republican primary and 70.2% in the general election) and took office in January 2017; he has represented the 5th District since January 2023 and was re-elected in 2024.

According to his House website, he serves on the Appropriations Committee's Homeland Security; Military Construction, Veterans Affairs; and Transportation, Housing and Urban Development subcommittees, and co-chairs several caucuses. Ballotpedia also lists him on the Committee on Ethics in the 119th Congress.

According to his congressional biography, he has been married to his wife, Pat, for 53 years; they have two children, six grandchildren, and three great-grandchildren and attend Assumption Catholic Church in Jacksonville.

priorities.text: Immigration: focuses on securing the border, streamlining the immigration process, and supporting border patrol agents.

Community Safety: says he is focused on keeping kids safe in school, families safe at home, and police safe on the job, drawing on more than 40 years of law-enforcement experience as a former sheriff.
Says the One Big Beautiful Bill Act delivers the largest tax cut in history for middle- and working-class Americans.

positions.summary: Sponsored the Protect and Serve Act increasing penalties for attacks on law enforcement officers, introduced H.R. 2379 to provide bulletproof vests for state and local law enforcement, and advocated for the School Resource Officer Act to hire additional school resource officers.
positions.quote: As a former Sheriff with over 40 years of law enforcement experience, nothing is more important to me than the safety and security of our community.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations and the Committee on Ethics in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Rachel Grage
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary over Alexander Hazen and Mark Heggestad.

summary.text: Rachel Grage is the Democratic nominee for Florida's 5th Congressional District. She describes herself as an engineer, health care professional, and mother of four, with engineering degrees from Tulane University. She ran for the Florida House in 2024 and is running on affordability, accountability, and protecting individual rights.

background.text: Earned bachelor's and master's degrees in engineering from Tulane University.
Worked as a biomedical engineer focused on improving health outcomes.
Has been affiliated with Catholic Charities, Equality Florida, and the Democratic Women's Club of Florida; says she has advocated on issues affecting Florida families.
Ran as the Democratic nominee for Florida House District 16 in 2024 and lost to incumbent Kiyan Michael, 39.3% to 60.7%.
Won the August 18, 2026 Democratic primary for the 5th District with 65.1% of the vote against Alexander Hazen and Mark Heggestad; describes herself as a mother of four.

priorities.text: Addressing rising costs for families, including health care premiums, insurance instability and housing affordability.
Protecting democracy, individual rights, due process and the rule of law.

statements.quote: Work to keep healthcare premiums and prescription costs affordable, maintain federal cost-sharing supports, and stabilize home insurance.
statements.context: On her campaign website, under "Lower Costs & Strengthen the Middle Class"

statements.quote: Ensure America's borders are secure through smart, efficient enforcement, while maintaining a fair and humane immigration system that respects due process.
statements.context: On her campaign website, under "Secure Borders & Fair Immigration"

candidates.researchNotes: Statements are from her campaign website and 2026 Ballotpedia survey. Neither states a position on abortion, guns, climate or other tracked issues in specific terms.

candidates.name: William Upham
candidates.ballotNote: Qualified as a write-in, no-party-affiliation candidate.

summary.text: William Upham is a write-in, no-party-affiliation candidate for Florida's 5th Congressional District. Jacksonville Today reports he is a former Marine and former state prosecutor who was arrested in July 2026 and charged with threatening the president; the charge is an allegation and he has not been convicted.

background.text: Jacksonville Today describes him as a former state prosecutor and a discharged U.S. Marine; the Marine Corps said he was medically discharged on May 30, 2025.
In a July 2026 video he said he decided to run to "fix our broken political system."

On July 16, 2026, the U.S. Attorney's Office announced he had been arrested and charged with threatening to kill President Trump, based on statements in two Facebook videos, according to the complaint. He appeared in federal court in Jacksonville and was detained; if convicted he faces up to five years in prison. The charge is unproven, and the report does not include a response from him.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Candidate Connection survey, or policy statements could be located for Upham; news coverage found concerned a campaign video, not issue positions.
